display.purpose: The home hero statement only. Archivo 600 with -0.035em tracking and text-wrap: balance. The research page runs its own hero at clamp(44px, 6.2vw, 72px).

headline.purpose: The page name printed in paper on the full-bleed fabric masthead.

title.purpose: Publication board titles. 19px on desktop, 17px below 640px. Every board is one size.

narrative.overview:
The site is a conference poster session, not a publication ledger. Three materials carry everything: the hall floor (#eef5f1, mint mist) you stand on, the board fabric (#d9ebe1, pale mint felt) you face, and the poster stock (#fbfdfc) pinned to it. Nothing else is a surface. The page ground is always the floor; a .board is only applied where a board actually stands (the header strip, a page masthead, the home hero); .stock is only applied to a sheet that is pinned to something. The fabric is pale mint felt: fractal noise in dark flecks over #d9ebe1, a material applied only where a board stands, never a page-wide grain.

Every publication board is the same size. Citation-sized tiers were part of the original rebuild and were removed at the lab's request in October 2026; papers are distinguished by track, by order, and by the home page's featured boards.

Colour is rationed hard. Harbor navy (#1d4a73) is the only action colour and the only colour the navigation strip is allowed; the eight research-topic hues were demoted from decoration to data and appear exclusively as small printed squares. Every corner is square. There is no monospace anywhere.
keyCharacteristics: Three materials only: hall floor, board fabric, poster stock.
Every publication board is one size; citations are a sort, not a scale.
One accent (harbor navy) for actions, board tags, and "you are here".
Topic hues are swatches, never text.
Zero border-radius; hairlines are inset rings, not borders.
Archivo for signage and headings, Literata for reading. No monospace.
Tabular figures globally — every number on the site is a measurement.

rules.name: The Swatch-Only Rule
rules.body: A track colour may only be a filled square of at most 0.65rem, or the stroke of a line illustration. It is never text colour, never a border, never a ground behind text. Audit test: five of the eight hues fail WCAG AA as text on the hall floor (#d97706 2.88:1, #0d9488 3.38:1, #0284c7 3.70:1, #db2777 4.15:1, #dc2626 4.36:1), so the rule is not a preference — it is the only way the taxonomy stays legible.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Navy is the site's only chromatic accent. If a new element needs to look important and is not an action, a board address, or the current destination, it gets weight or inversion, not colour.

rules.name: The 4.5 Floor
rules.body: Every text-on-ground pair ships at 4.5:1 or better and the measured number is recorded. Paper at 72% over fabric (#c5c8c9, used for nav destinations and the header tagline) sits at 4.76:1; the masthead lede uses 78% (5.26:1). An earlier tint failed AA and had to be replaced, so treat these percentages as floors, not as styling knobs.

rules.name: The No-Mono Rule
rules.body: Years, citation counts, board numbers, and filter counts are measurements, not code. font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums is set on html, so Archivo's tabular figures align them in columns. Never introduce a monospace face to make something look technical.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Archivo speaks for the hall (signage, headings, labels, controls); Literata speaks for the sheet (anything set with .read). A block does not switch voice mid-way, and a caption never gets the serif.

rules.name: The 68ch Rule
rules.body: Reading text is capped at 64ch by .read; the masthead lede at 52ch; the research hero lede at 36ch. A paragraph that has no measure cap is a bug.

rules.name: The Pinned-Sheet Rule
rules.body: Depth exists only where paper meets fabric. If a surface is not a sheet, it is flat: filter chips, buttons, stamps, and nav destinations get inversion or a 1px rule, never a shadow.

rules.name: The Square Rule
rules.body: Border-radius is 0. A rounded pill or a rounded card is out of world; if an element needs to feel lighter, reduce its weight or its contrast, not its corners.

rules.name: The One Size Rule
rules.body: Every board is the same size. Do not size boards by citations or resize one by hand to promote it: feature a paper with highlight, and leave impact to the Most cited sort.

rules.name: The Unnumbered Host Rule
rules.body: The navy 01-style tag addresses the work. The lab's own board on the home page deliberately carries no number; featured boards are addressed from 01 upward.

rules.name: The Sub-Head Address Rule
rules.body: The numbered kicker (an inverted-ink number plus the track name) sits below its h3, never above it. A small label above a heading is banned outright; the same content reads as an address when it follows the headline.

dos: Do put a new surface on one of the three materials: hall floor, .board fabric, or .stock paper. Anything else is out of world.
Do bleed fabric to 100vw with .board-bleed and keep its words in a nested max-w-5xl px-6 wrapper.
Do express a topic colour as a filled square of at most 0.65rem, with the label beside it in --color-ink or --color-ink-faint.
Do record the measured contrast ratio when introducing a new text/ground pair, and keep it at 4.5:1 or better.
Do use .read for anything a visitor reads in sentences, and leave scanned text in Archivo.
Do reach for weight, size, or inversion (ink ground / paper text) when something needs emphasis — that is this system's entire emphasis vocabulary.
Do use an inset ring (inset 0 0 0 1px) for hairlines so a border never shifts layout.
Do gate any autoplay or transform behind prefers-reduced-motion.
donts: Don't use a track colour as text, as a border, or as a ground behind text.
Don't add a second accent. Navy is the only chromatic action colour.
Don't introduce a monospace face. Tabular Archivo figures are already the answer for numbers.
Don't put a small uppercase label or eyebrow above a heading. If the content is needed, it goes below the heading as a kicker.
Don't round anything. No pills, no rounded cards, no rounded buttons.
Don't ship gradient text, a coloured border-left callout, or any glass / backdrop-blur decoration.
Don't apply the .stock shadow to a control, a chip, or a fabric band.
Don't apply the fabric weave as a page-wide texture; it belongs only where a board actually is.
Don't resize a publication board, by hand or by citations. Every board is one size.
Don't stack four or five type sizes inside a single board to create hierarchy.
